[GENERATED IMPLEMENTATION]
import Lean
import Lean.Data.String

@[inline] def parse_number (s: String) : Nat :=
  match s.trim with
  | String.nil => 0
  | s' => let (num, rest) := s'.parseNum;
          if rest.is_empty then num else 0

def implementation (string: String) (n: Nat) : Nat :=
  let apples := parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_left);
  let oranges := parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_right);
  n - apples - oranges
[END]
[HELPER LEMMAS]
lemma parse_number_zero (s: String) (h: s.trim = String.nil) : parse_number s = 0 :=
by simp [s, h]

lemma parse_number_correct (s: String) (n: Nat) (h: s.trim = n.repr) : parse_number s = n :=
by simp [s, h]

lemma split_correct_left (s: String) (sep: String) (h: s.split sep.get_left = s.trim) :
  s.split sep.get_left = s.trim :=
by simp [s, sep, h]

lemma split_correct_right (s: String) (sep: String) (h: s.split sep.get_right = s.trim) :
  s.split sep.get_right = s.trim :=
by simp [s, sep, h]
[END]
[PROOF]
by
unfold problem_spec
let result := implementation string n
use result
simp [result]
simp [implementation]
existsi (parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_left)), (parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_right))
simp [string.split " apples and ".get_left, string.split " apples and ".get_right]
split
-- proving x + y = n - result
let x := parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_left);
let y := parse_number (string.split " apples and ".get_right);
let h_x_y_eq_n_minus_result := by
  simp [x, y, result]
  rw [Int.add_sub_cancel' (by linarith)]
  simp [Int.ofNat_add_ofNat_eq_ofNat_add_ofNat]
  linarith
exact h_x_y_eq_n_minus_result
-- proving string.join [x.repr, " apples and ", y.repr, " oranges"] = string
let x' := x.repr;
let y' := y.repr;
have h_x_y_repr := by
  simp [x, y, x', y']
